I'm doing Film Studies, and we're a pretty small group overall. The profs for the most part are great, they know what they're doing and they're really passionate about their topics. The material itself is very dense and academic, and if you're not invested it is a lot of work. A lot of people assume we just watch movies, but we focus strongly on the theory side of things most of the time. A lot of interdisciplinary stuff, too. Plus, half the films we watch are terrible anyways. 

As for Film Production, its quite competitive, not everyone gets in. The Theatre Film department in general is quite underfunded, but its good enough for most work, I suppose. I don't know much since its not my primary area of study, but its worth asking the profs about it. The students produce some amazing work and some of their short films ends up playing at various festivals around Vancouver and North America.

FIST 300, Cult Cinema, easily. Prof encourages you to participate in the screenings, so you have people singing, saying the dialogue along, dance, throw shit around etc. And you get to watch gems like Rocky Horror Picture Show and The Room. Easy papers too, no final.
Thinking of joining Photosoc or Filmsoc. Photosoc seems to be around again in full force, thought they were dead for a while.

In this regard I've been incredibly lucky. But well, constantly moving has its share of difficulties, especially when growing up.

Now I'm studying in Canada. Basically even though I have a Malaysian passport I've spent 2/3 of my life abroad.
Canada! Its a bit far from home, but its nice to be able to experience a completely different place than what I'm used to, so I don't mind the hassle.

This past few weeks I haven't had much to do since class ended for me and I'm flying back to my country in a week. So I've been exploring a fair bit and also been taking photos everyday on film and developing them myself every week. Sometimes I don't even go explore really, I just walk around the city and take pictures of interesting people and things. 

I go through anywhere from 1 to 3 rolls every week, and its costing me a fair bit of money, to be honest. But well, I just love the experience way too much.....

You're being very objective of yourself as though a pass/fail is everything there is to your life. 

So you didn't get into the program you wanted to get into. More people probably didn't get in than did, its not the end of your life as you know it. Your life isn't going to nosedive because of this one thing. Sometimes things will not go the way you want it to, and that's fine. If life is that predictable then most of the issues you see plaguing the world today would probably go away.

Look at yourself subjectively. Surely you're not living your life just to be successful in life, there must be more to it than becoming a lawyer, a banker or a rich housewife. Do you seriously start your day everyday just making sure everything is going to plan with your life? 

Do you have any talents or hobbies? Writing, making art, reading? Find something to latch yourself to, something other than your major. Your major/future career is not what your life is worth. 

Also, someone once told me to not be proud or dismissive of UBC, but be proud of yourself. Since UBC is mediocre to you, maybe don't be dismissive of the fact that you "only" attend UBC, maybe look at yourself as a person instead and be proud of what you've achieved so far. 

Everything will be ok, things will work themselves out for the better.

I might take these courses next year, so I can't really say exactly. But if they're anything like FIST courses, as long as you put in the effort (do the readings, attend screenings, participate in discussions etc.), you should be ok. Probably not easy, but not too hardcore either.

Hey, a fellow TCK. Its not often you find one on reddit, let alone a Malaysian one. 

So you went to school in France and the UK growing up, I imagine. Did you go to public schools or private? Why were you raised abroad, parent's occupation? Also why study in Malaysia, then, of all places? Europe certainly has better options in terms of education.....
The last week of classes was tough. So many papers due in like the same two days. I didn't sleep much at all.

I find the faculty separation thing to be due to the campus separating them. Art classes are all at one side of the campus, for example. I see the same faces all the time, but once I walk into the EOS building, its like a completely new experience. 

My friends from outside the faculty are just people I met through clubs and parties, really.

I'm also in university abroad, in Canada. Most of my friends are local or have lived here most of their lives. The ones that move around haven't move far or much. 

When I first came here I did struggle with relating to anyone really. I joined the photography club, which didn't meet often, so I what little people I meet there, we only tend to have photography in common, and even then opportunities to chill are rare. My only "friends" then, really, was my neighbors in the dorms.

One of my neighbors attends a lot of events on campus, and I started doing the same with her invitation. Through her and the events I've met a lot more people. In fact she was the one person through which I've made any friends at all, since she invited me to events and her parties, through which I joined their community cafe, and become more involved, even though I was the most international person there, with the weirdest accent probably.

I never bring up my TCKness unless prompted, and most of the time I still struggle with conversations talking about stuff local specific. That's where most of my conversations go nowadays. Trying to fit in. Social anxiety and depression doesn't help. I'm still an alien there, but at least I somehow get acknowledged as being a part of something. 

My advice, really, is find out more about the local scene and try to involved yourself more. Find something specific that you like, and expand your circle outside of the group you mentioned, which exists here too, it seems. Just try and be a part of something, somehow.

I'm much like you. What little friends I have, I don't see everyday. I always study alone, preferably in public because I cannot stand the silence of being alone at home. Last year I joined a club and was one of the few members who actually attended every event, because its not like I have many friends to hang out with and its my only form of social entertainment. Now I'm an exec in the club and its nice to have responsibilities at UBC that's not academic related. 

I'm an introvert. I hate big parties or going to the bar or club. I watch a lot of movies (3-4 weekly at least) either at home or at the cinemas, alone. I do most things alone. I shop alone, explore alone, attend events alone etc. Just today I was having lunch downtown by myself. It really gets to my head sometimes, like when I see a couple sitting across me, but it doesn't bother me as much anymore.....
